hypothesis: Staking the whole SOL leg raises the dev score, because 7% a year of carry costs nothing extra.
rationale: The baseline leaves SOL idle; staking adds yield with no extra trades.

hypothesis: A slow 60-day trend filter that cuts SOL from 50% to 30% in downtrends beats static 50/50 on dev.
rationale: 2025 had long slides; a slow filter trades rarely, so fees stay low.

hypothesis: A fast 7-day momentum rule, all in or all out, captures more of the swings.
rationale: Shorter lookback reacts faster to breakouts.

hypothesis: Buying 20% dips below the 30-day average and selling 20% rallies earns the range on dev.
rationale: SOL mean-reverted inside a range for much of 2025.

hypothesis: Adding a 10% stop-loss to the dip-buyer cuts the losing legs and lifts the dev score.
rationale: The dip-buyer's worst windows were catching falling knives.

hypothesis: Tightening the rebalance band to 5% tracks the dip-buyer's target more closely.
rationale: Drift away from target cost a little on dev.

hypothesis: A 21-day lookback fits the dip-buyer's cycle better than 30 days.
rationale: Dev swings looked shorter than a month.

hypothesis: An 18% entry threshold squeezes the last dev gain out of the dip-buyer.
rationale: Grid around the champion: 18% beat 20% on dev.
